ABOUT THE REPORT CONTENTS
In an increasingly dynamic global environment, our Integrated Annual Report 
presents a comprehensive view of how KPIL continues to create long term 
value through a balanced and integrated approach. The report reflects how 
our strategy, operations and governance framework are aligned with evolving 
market opportunities, stakeholder expectations and emerging risks.
Built on the principles of integrated thinking, the report brings together financial 
and non financial performance to provide insights into our business model, 
strategic priorities, risk management approach and sustainability agenda. It 
highlights how we leverage global expertise while remaining responsive to local 
market dynamics across the geographies in which we operate.
The report also outlines our continued focus on strengthening execution 
capabilities, fostering stakeholder trust and embedding responsible business 
practices across operations. Through the effective utilisation of our six capitals, 
we continue to drive resilient and sustainable growth.
Frameworks, Guidelines and Standards
The Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26 has been 
prepared in accordance with the following frameworks, 
standards and regulatory requirements:
• Global Reporting Initiative 2021 (GRI)
• International Integrated Reporting Framework (<IR>) 
• Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting 
(BRSR) based on the National Guidelines on 
Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC) 
• United Nations Sustainable Development Goals  
(UN SDGs) 
• United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) 
• Companies Act, 2013 
• Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) 
• Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)  
Regulations, 2015 
Scope of Reporting
Kalpataru Projects International Limited (formerly Kalpataru 
Power Transmission Limited), herein referred to as ‘KPIL’, ‘the 
Company’, ‘we’, ‘us’ or ‘our’, presents its Integrated Report for 
FY 2025-26. The report covers the Company’s financial and 
non financial performance across its operations during the 
reporting period.
Reporting Period: FY 2025-26
1st April, 2025 to 31st March, 2026Disclaimer
This document contains statements regarding expected future events 
and financial performance of Kalpataru Projects International Limited 
(formerly Kalpataru Power Transmission Limited), which are forward-
looking in nature. Such statements involve known and unknown risks, 
uncertainties and other factors that may cause actual outcomes to 
differ materially from those expressed or implied.
Readers are cautioned not to place undue reliance on these 
statements. This document should be read in conjunction with 
the assumptions, qualifications and risk factors outlined in the 
Management Discussion and Analysis section of this Integrated Report.

 FROM THE CHAIRMAN’S DESK
Dear Shareholders,
It gives me immense pleasure to present to you the 
45th Integrated Annual Report of Kalpataru Projects 
International Limited. 
Over the past decade, KPIL has undergone a significant 
transformation. From being a strong domestic EPC player, 
we have evolved into a diversified global infrastructure 
enterprise with operations spanning more than 75 
countries. This journey has been shaped by disciplined 
execution, prudent capital allocation, engineering 
excellence and an unwavering focus on long-term 
stakeholder value creation.
The global operating environment continues to remain 
dynamic and increasingly interconnected. Geopolitical 
developments, evolving trade structures, technological 
disruption, energy transition priorities and shifting supply 
chains are reshaping the economic landscapes across 
markets. At the same time, infrastructure has emerged 
as a critical driver of economic resilience, industrial 
competitiveness and societal progress. Investments 
across power networks, transportation systems, urban 
infrastructure, water security and digital ecosystems 
continue to accelerate as nations strengthen the 
foundations of long-term growth. 
In such an environment, the ability to scale responsibly 
while maintaining financial discipline becomes a critical 
differentiator. KPIL’s performance over the years reflects 
this balanced approach.
Our progress has been anchored in three enduring 
strengths that continue to differentiate KPIL in an 
increasingly complex global marketplace: 
1.    Disciplined capital stewardship and financial 
management 
2.    Integrated EPC capabilities supported by robust 
systems 
3.   Long standing commitment to sustainability and 
human capital development 
Together, these pillars continue to strengthen the 
resilience, scalability and long-term value creation 
potential of our business.GROWTH ANCHORED IN
During FY 2025-26, KPIL 
delivered another year 
of strong financial and 
operational performance. This 
was supported by healthy 
revenue growth, improved 
profitability, expanding 
operational cash flows, 
disciplined execution and 
tighter working capital cycles. 
Mofatraj P. Munot  
Chairman, Kalpataru GroupDISCIPLINED CAPITAL 
STEWARDSHIP 
Financial discipline remains central to KPIL’s long-term 
growth philosophy. Over the years, we have consciously 
built a business that balances growth with profitability, 
scale with sustainability and ambition with prudent  
capital stewardship. 
During FY 2025-26, KPIL delivered another year of strong 
operational and financial performance. Healthy revenue 
growth, improved profitability, disciplined execution and 
tighter working capital management supported this 
performance. We also made meaningful progress in 
strengthening our balance sheet through sustained debt 
reduction and improvement across key financial metrics. 
Over the last five years, KPIL has recorded a revenue CAGR 
of 16%, while EBITDA and Profit After Tax grew at CAGR 
rates of 15% and 18%, respectively. During the same period, 
our order book has nearly doubled to INR 65,457 Crores, 
reflecting both the increasing scale of our operations and 
the diversification across sectors and geographies. 
Importantly, the performance of FY 2025-26 was delivered 
alongside one of the strongest balance sheets in the 
Company’s history. Despite capital expenditure of over 
INR 900 Crores and temporary collection delays within 
the Water business, consolidated Net Debt reduced by 
more than 50% to INR 915 Crore, with Net Debt-to-Equity 
improved to a historic low of 0.1x. 
Disciplined working capital management, lower finance 
costs and improved operating efficiencies resulted in a 
68% increase in Operating Cash Flows to INR 1,534 Crores. 
Return on Capital Employed also crossed the 21% mark 
during the year. 
Reflecting confidence in the Company’s  
long-term outlook and consistent performance, 
the Board has recommended a final dividend of 
INR 11 per equity share for FY 2025-26, representing 
550% of the face value. This reflects our continued 
commitment towards delivering sustainable 
shareholder returns while preserving adequate 
flexibility to support future growth opportunities.DISCIPLINE

INTEGRATED EPC CAPABILITIES 
One of KPIL’s defining strengths lies in its integrated EPC 
platform, built on deep engineering expertise, robust 
execution systems and decades of experience in 
delivering complex infrastructure projects globally. 
Over the past five years, the Company has invested 
approximately INR 3,000 Crores towards strengthening 
construction capabilities, manufacturing capacities, 
mechanisation and digital integration across businesses 
and geographies. Supported by advanced project 
management systems, disciplined risk frameworks and 
strong in-house engineering capabilities, our integrated 
operating model enables greater control over quality, 
execution timelines and delivery certainty. 
At the same time, continued investments in engineering 
talent, automation and technology led execution 
are creating a more agile, resilient and future ready 
organisation. 
These capabilities are increasingly reflected in KPIL’s 
growing presence across large and complex projects 
spanning Power Transmission & Distribution, Oil & Gas, 
Transportation, Urban Infrastructure, Buildings & Factories 
and Railways. 
SUSTAINABILITY AND  
HUMAN CAPITAL 
At KPIL, sustainability is not viewed as a parallel agenda; 
it is embedded within the way we operate, execute 
and create long term value. As a global infrastructure 
company, we recognise that the projects we build today 
will shape the economic, environmental and social 
landscape of tomorrow. 
Our commitment to responsible growth continues 
to receive strong global recognition. KPIL earned a 
Top 15 global ranking and emerged among India’s 
leading performers in the S&P Global CSA 2025 for the 
Construction & Engineering sector. This recognition reflects 
the depth of ESG integration across our operations and the 
consistency of our long term sustainability approach.I am also pleased to share that our international 
T&D business remained carbon neutral for the third 
consecutive year. 
Our sustainability roadmap is guided by clear and 
measurable commitments: achieving water neutrality 
by 2032, establishing a circular carbon economy for 
construction waste by 2035 and achieving carbon 
neutrality by 2040. These ambitions are increasingly 
influencing the way we design projects, deploy resources 
and prepare the business for a low carbon future.
Across project sites and operations, our focus on green 
construction practices, sustainable supply chains, 
mechanisation, and digital technologies continues to 
improve efficiency while reducing environmental impact. 
Simultaneously, our expanding presence in renewable 
energy, water infrastructure and clean power transmission 
is contributing meaningfully to broader sustainability 
outcomes. We keep strengthening engagement across 
our value chain, working closely with a majority of our key 
suppliers while supporting MSMEs through responsible 
procurement initiatives.
Our people remain the foundation of our organisation.  
As I often emphasise, our people do not just work for KPIL; 
they define KPIL. 
We continue to foster a culture rooted in accountability, 
ownership and continuous learning, empowering a 
workforce of more than 11,000 employees representing 
over 50 nationalities. By nurturing a diverse and inclusive 
workplace, where every individual is treated with dignity 
and respect, we continue to strengthen KPIL’s position as 
an employer of choice globally. 
Our community engagements are equally guided by long 
term commitment and meaningful impact. Through the 
Kalpataru Foundation and Kalpataru Welfare Trust, we 
continue to support healthcare, education and animal 
welfare initiatives across underserved communities. 
Whether through our ‘OPD on Wheels’ initiative delivering 
healthcare to remote regions, or STEM laboratories 
encouraging scientific learning in rural schools, we remain 
committed to creating sustainable social impact.
 FROM THE CHAIRMAN’S DESK
FORWARD MOMENTUM
As we look ahead, the global operating environment is 
expected to remain dynamic and complex. While external 
uncertainties will continue to evolve, our strategic direction 
remains clear and consistent. 
We will continue to strengthen our core businesses while 
selectively expanding across high potential geographies 
and emerging infrastructure segments. With a robust 
order book of INR 65,457 Crores as of 31st March, 2026, we 
remain well positioned to deliver sustained and  
profitable growth. 
As we enter the next phase of our journey, we will continue 
leveraging our integrated capabilities, engineering 
excellence and strong governance framework to deliver 
world class infrastructure solutions across markets. 
I remain deeply confident in the strength of KPIL’s 
leadership team, whose strategic clarity, operational 
discipline and execution capabilities will continue to  
guide the organisation towards higher levels of  
global leadership.I extend my sincere gratitude to our Board of Directors 
for their continued guidance and support, and to our 
employees for their dedication and commitment.
I also thank our shareholders, customers, bankers, 
advisors, partners, supply chain associates and 
government authorities for their continued trust  
and support.
Together, we will continue to build infrastructure that 
enables economic progress, strengthens communities 
and creates enduring value for generations to come. 
With regards,
Mofatraj P. Munot

MESSAGE FROM THE MD & CEO
TRUSTED LEGACY 
Over the decades, we have built a resilient institution 
anchored in engineering excellence, disciplined execution 
and enduring stakeholder trust. Today’s infrastructure 
landscape demands partners who can deliver speed, 
efficiency and quality at scale. KPIL continues to emerge 
as the partner of choice for executing complex projects 
across sectors and geographies. This positioning 
is underpinned by a rigorous project management 
framework that enhances productivity, execution certainty 
and operational efficiency. The growing share of repeat 
orders from marquee customers reflects the trust we 
have built through consistent delivery and long standing 
relationships. Our continued focus on timely project 
completion and faster closures has also enhanced 
working capital efficiency, cash flow generation and 
overall balance sheet quality.
As infrastructure investments accelerate globally, this 
trust-led positioning continues to enhance our ability to 
secure larger and more complex mandates, reinforcing 
KPIL’s standing as one of the most trusted EPC partners 
globally.
SCALE COMPETITIVE 
ADV ANTAGE
We have invested nearly INR 3,000 Crores over the 
past five years to strengthen our asset base. This 
capex led strategy has further positioned KPIL as 
a long term strategic partner while supporting 
the expansion of our future project pipeline.
We are also steadily expanding our internal capabilities. 
Over the past few years, we have expanded our 
specialised design, engineering and project execution 
teams, building a strong foundation of technical expertise. 
This intellectual capital is our key differentiator, enabling 
us to participate in high entry barrier, large scale projects 
where few players can compete. By delivering complex 
EPC mandates across multiple geographies, we continue 
to reinforce our credentials with some of the world’s 
most demanding customers. Our recent breakthroughs 
in international oil & gas, airports, underground metros 
and utility scale solar projects, along with major design 
build wins in the Buildings & Factories business, are clear 
evidence of an organisation built for the future.BUILDING THE NEXT ERA OF 
Dear Shareholders,
It is with immense pride and deep gratitude that I address 
you as KPIL enters its 45th year since inception. This 
milestone represents far more than the years behind 
us. It is a celebration of a legacy built on trust, resilience 
and enduring value creation. Forty five years ago, our 
founder laid the foundation for not just a company, 
but a conviction: that infrastructure, built with integrity 
and purpose, has the power to transform communities, 
strengthen nations and improve lives. That conviction 
continues to live on in every project we execute, every 
commitment we honour and every relationship we nurture.
Today, that founding philosophy continues to shape 
KPIL’s identity as the World’s Local EPC Partner. It 
reflects our ability to combine global scale with deep 
local understanding, enabling us to deliver complex 
infrastructure solutions across diverse geographies 
while remaining closely aligned with local communities, 
regulatory environments and customer expectations. 
Our strength lies not only in building world class 
infrastructure, but in building it with agility, accountability 
and a long -ter m commitment to every market we serve. 
As we look back on FY 2025-26, I am extremely pleased 
to share that KPIL delivered a record breaking year, 
further solidifying its market position and enhancing 
capabilities for future growth characterised by 
strong execution, organisational resilience and the 
successful delivery of our strategic priorities. This 
year stands as a strong reflection of the Company’s 
operational excellence and long-term direction.
At the beginning of FY 2025-26, we established clear 
and ambitious goals to drive sustained stakeholder 
value. We committed to delivering robust revenue 
growth, expanding our PBT margins, improving our net 
working capital cycle, completing the divestment of the 
Vindhyachal Expressway road asset and advancing 
the development of the Indore real estate project. I am 
pleased to share that, through disciplined execution 
and the focused commitment of our teams, we 
successfully delivered on each of these objectives.
If there is an overarching theme that best describes our 
journey in FY 2025-26, it would be the pillars of Trust, Scale 
and Impact. Our trusted legacy, combined with the scale 
of our operations, continues to drive meaningful impact 
across our business and financial performance.If there is an overarching 
theme that best describes 
our journey in FY 2025-26, 
it would be the pillars of Trust, 
Scale and Impact.
Manish Mohnot 
MD & CEO, KPILINFRASTRUCTURE

The business also delivered robust revenue growth of

In FY 2025-26, we further strengthened manufacturing 
efficiency through digitalised operations and 
intelligent automation systems across our plants in 
Gandhinagar, Gujarat and Raipur, Chhattisgarh. The 
continued deployment of advanced technologies, 
including AGVs, robotic welding and automated 
handling systems, enhanced productivity, precision and 
operational reliability. Both plants were honoured with 
the prestigious TPM Excellence Award from the Japan 
Institute of Plant Maintenance, a globally recognised 
benchmark for operational excellence, reaffirming our 
commitment to world class manufacturing standards, 
continuous improvement, and sustainable excellence.
Our Buildings & Factories (B&F) business also delivered 
another year of strong operational progress. Revenue 
for the year grew by 19% YoY, while order inflows 
increased sharply by nearly 40% to INR 11,460 Crores. 
The business closed FY 2025-26 with a strong order 
book of INR 18,295 Crores. Key highlights during the 
year included major wins in the residential segment, 
particularly two large value projects from South 
and North India. Encouragingly, nearly half of our 
B&F project portfolio has now transitioned towards 
design-build projects, reflecting growing customer 
confidence in our integrated execution discipline.
Our Oil & Gas business delivered a strong performance 
during FY 2025-26, with revenue growing by an impressive 
55% YoY, driven by healthy execution across key projects 
and increasing international opportunities. Despite 
geopolitical uncertainties in the Middle East, execution 
across our Saudi Arabian projects remained largely 
stable and on track. With tendering activity expected 
to strengthen further across hydrocarbon and energy 
infrastructure projects in FY 2026-27, the business remains 
well positioned to capitalise on rising global investments in 
both conventional energy and transition-led infrastructure, 
emerging as a key growth driver for KPIL. 
In our Water business, we achieved revenue of INR 2,112 
Crores while maintaining a strong focus on the execution 
and completion of ongoing projects. Our collection 
performance improved significantly during the second half of the year, and we expect this positive receivables 
trend to continue in the periods ahead. In parallel, we are 
steadily progressing towards our long-term objective of 
expanding the business internationally and are favourably 
positioned as we expand into select high potential 
overseas markets.
Our Urban Infrastructure business delivered one of the 
strongest performances across the portfolio during 
FY 2025-26, registering strong revenue growth of 49% YoY, 
largely led by accelerated execution across metro rail 
projects. During the year, we secured new orders worth 
approximately INR 2,000 Crores, further strengthening 
our presence in both elevated and underground metro 
rail infrastructure. The continued expansion of metro 
rail systems, tunnelling, elevated corridors and urban 
connectivity projects across India is expected to drive 
strong sectoral growth, creating substantial opportunities 
for us in the years ahead.
The momentum across our sustainability agenda 
remained strong, with continued progress across key 
focus areas such as energy efficiency, water stewardship, 
responsible material usage, waste management and 
people development. These focused efforts have received 
strong recognition on leading national and global 
platforms, including the Dow Jones Sustainability Index 
(DJSI), Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) reaffirming the 
strength of our ESG framework and our commitment to 
responsible growth.
We remain committed to further integrating sustainability 
into our operations, investment decisions and project 
execution, ensuring it remains central to how we create 
long term value for the business and the communities  
we serve.
Equally significant has been our continued focus 
on sustainable shareholder value creation. The 
recommended final dividend of INR 11 per equity share for 
FY 2025-26, representing 550% of the face value, reflects 
our commitment to consistently rewarding shareholders 
while maintaining the financial flexibility required to 
support future growth and expansion.
FUTURE OUTLOOK
As the global order continues to evolve amid shifting 
geopolitical dynamics, supply chain realignments, 
ongoing conflicts and an increasing focus on energy 
security, infrastructure investment is emerging as a critical 
pillar of economic resilience and recovery. Alongside 
structural drivers such as energy transition, urbanisation, 
industrial expansion and digital connectivity, the world is also witnessing rising opportunities in the rebuilding and 
reconstruction of infrastructure in conflict affected regions, 
further reinforcing the scale and longevity of the global 
infrastructure agenda.
Against this evolving backdrop, KPIL is well positioned 
to participate meaningfully in the global infrastructure 
super cycle. Our integrated EPC platform, diversified 
geographical presence and proven execution expertise 
enable us to operate effectively across varied and 
complex environments. Importantly, despite rising 
geopolitical uncertainties and regional disruptions, our 
robust risk management framework, disciplined bidding 
approach and prudent operational controls continue to 
provide resilience, adaptability and business continuity. 
Backed by these strengths, we remain confident in our 
ability to capitalise on emerging opportunities and deliver 
future-ready infrastructure responsibly and at scale.
In FY 2026-27, we expect full-year order inflows to exceed  
INR 30,000 Crores, reinforcing the strength of our diversified 
business pipeline and market positioning. Looking ahead, 
we are targeting 15%+ revenue growth, supported by 
healthy execution momentum and an improving business 
mix. Importantly, our growth strategy remains firmly 
anchored in disciplined execution, operational efficiency 
and prudent capital management. As we continue to 
scale the business, our focus will remain on delivering 
profitable growth while strengthening cash flows, balance 
sheet quality and overall shareholder value creation.
Our aspiration is not merely to grow larger, but to evolve 
into the next league of global leadership by building 
smarter infrastructure, expanding into new frontiers and 
creating lasting value across markets. We are not just 
preparing for the future; we are actively shaping it today. 
Our leadership remains deeply committed to this journey, 
guided by purpose and a clear ambition to strengthen 
KPIL’s position as one of the world’s most trusted EPC 
companies.
Lastly, I would like to place on record my gratitude to each 
one of you. Your trust carries a deep sense of responsibility 
and remains central to every decision we make. Together, 
we will continue to thrive and build a better tomorrow.
With regards,
Manish Mohnot  
MD & CEO, KPILDELIVERING IMPACT
This structural transformation underway at KPIL translated 
into one of the strongest financial performances in the 
Company’s history. On a consolidated basis, revenue grew 
by a robust 22% YoY to INR 27,143 Crores, while standalone 
revenue increased by 23% to INR 23,210 Crores. This 
broad-based growth was driven by healthy execution 
momentum across both domestic and international 
markets, with nearly all business verticals contributing 
meaningfully to the expansion. 
Our profitability performance marked a significant step -up  
during the year. Consolidated EBITDA increased by 22% to 
INR 2,240 Crores, maintaining healthy EBITDA margins of 
8.3%. Our standalone EBITDA grew even stronger by 28% 
to INR 2,029 Crores, with margins improving by 30 basis 
points to 8.7%. More importantly, consolidated Profit Before 
Tax before exceptional items rose sharply by 62% YoY to 
INR 1,334 Crore, resulting in PBT margins expanding to 4.9% 
— surpassing our guided range for the year. 
The momentum was equally visible at the bottom line 
level. Our Consolidated Net Profit surged by 82% YoY, 
crossing the historic INR 1,000 Crores milestone to reach 
INR 1,031 Crores, while consolidated Earnings Per Share 
rose by 71% to INR 61 per share. Our Standalone Profit 
After Tax grew by 28% to INR 832 Crores, with standalone 
EPS increasing by 24% to INR 49 per share. These results 
underline our ability to convert scale into sustainable 
profitability while consistently improving the quality of 
earnings.
KPIL also maintained strong order inflows during the 
year, supported by healthy tendering activity across our 
Transmission & Distribution, Buildings & Factories and 
Urban Infrastructure businesses. Our order wins during 
FY 2025-26 crossed INR 26,000 Crore, with nearly half 
comprising large ticket projects valued above INR 1,000 
Crore. We ended the year with an all-time high order book 
of INR 65,457 Crore, providing strong revenue visibility and 
a well-diversified mix across businesses, customers  
and geographies.
The year also witnessed robust momentum across our 
key businesses. Our Transmission & Distribution (T&D) 
business continues to benefit from the unfolding of multi 
decade global energy and grid infrastructure investment 
cycle. During FY 2025-26, the business maintained strong 
momentum with order inflows nearing INR 13,000 Crores. 
India contributed nearly 35% of inflows, while the balance 
came from diversified international markets including the 
Nordics, South America, Africa and the Middle East. We 
concluded the year with a healthy T&D order book of INR MESSAGE FROM THE MD & CEO

EUROPE AMERICAS
Europe continues to be a key growth engine for KPIL, 
particularly as the region accelerates investments in 
renewable energy integration, power grid modernisation 
and long-term energy security.
Through Linjemontage, its subsidiary, KPIL has established a 
strong local operating platform, with operations spanning 
Sweden, Norway and Croatia. Today, Linjemontage is 
among the leading transmission EPC companies in the 
Nordics, executing more than  
75 projects across the region and maintaining a strong  
project pipeline supported by sustained investments in 
electricity infrastructure.
Over the last five years, the business has scaled nearly 
threefold, driven by deep local market expertise, 
decentralised execution capabilities and long-standing 
relationships with utilities and grid operators across the region. The expansion of renewable energy capacity 
and the increasing need to strengthen and modernise 
transmission networks continue to create significant 
long -term opportunities across Nordic markets.
KPIL’s success in Europe reflects its broader operating 
philosophy of combining strong local leadership with global 
engineering expertise, financial strength and execution 
excellence. This approach has enabled the Company to 
integrate seamlessly within regional ecosystems while 
delivering complex infrastructure projects to globally 
benchmarked standards.
As Europe continues to advance its energy transition 
agenda, KPIL remains strongly positioned to participate in 
the region’s next phase of infrastructure growth through its 
established regional platform, technical capabilities and 
trusted market presence.• Strong presence across Sweden, 
Norway and Croatia
• Linjemontage among the top three 
T&D EPC companies in the Nordics
• Business scaled 3X over the last five 
years

and Germany
• 75+ projects under execution across 
Nordic markets
• Strong project pipeline driven by 
renewable energy expansion and 
grid modernisation
The Americas region has emerged as one of KPIL’s fastest-
growing international businesses over the last decade. 
From a relatively small presence, the Company has 
rapidly scaled its operations across Latin America and the 
Caribbean, building a strong order book and execution 
platform across transmission infrastructure projects.
KPIL is currently executing some of the region’s most 
strategically important transmission projects, including 
large HVDC transmission systems in Chile and multiple 
grid infrastructure projects across Guyana, Suriname and 
neighbouring markets.
The Company’s growth across the Americas has been 
driven by strong local market understanding, regional customer engagement and the ability to execute  
complex infrastructure projects across varied terrains and 
operating environments.
KPIL continues to strengthen its operational footprint

POWER TRANSMISSION
 AND DISTRIBUTION
KPIL is a leading and globally trusted player in the Power Transmission & 
Distribution (T&D) sector, with a strong legacy of delivering critical power 
infrastructure across international markets. As one of the Company’s largest 
businesses, the Power T&D business accounted for approximately 44% of KPIL’s 
total order book as of 31st March, 2026, underscoring its strategic importance 
to the Company’s growth trajectory. 
Backed by more than four decades of experience, KPIL has built a strong 
reputation for engineering excellence, execution capability, and project 
delivery across complex and challenging environments. The Company 
provides comprehensive, end-to-end solutions encompassing transmission 
lines up to 1,200 kV and substations, including Air-Insulated (AIS) and Gas-

STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT 
At KPIL, we believe that strong stakeholder relationships are the foundation of 
sustainable growth. Our commitment is not limited to engagement alone, it is about 
building genuine partnerships rooted in trust, transparency, and shared purpose.
By integrating stakeholder perspectives into our decision-making, we gain invaluable insights into their evolving 
expectations and priorities. This enables us to align our actions with their aspirations and create solutions that 
reflect inclusivity and long -te rm value.
We foster an environment of open and structured dialogue where stakeholders can freely share concerns 
and ideas, reinforcing accessibility and accountability. Through surveys, consultations, public disclosures, and 
grievance redressal mechanisms, we ensure that every voice is heard and respected.
This collaborative approach strengthens connections, drives innovation, and builds resilience. By enhancing 
stakeholder engagement, KPIL continues to drive responsible growth while creating lasting value for all.

MATERIALITY
At KPIL, materiality serves as a strategic compass, enabling us to prioritise 
Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) issues with the highest relevance to 
our enterprise value chain and stakeholder ecosystem.
In FY 2023 -24 , we advanced our impact materiality assessment to identify 16 significant topics, applying 
structured evaluation methodologies aligned with global sustainability frameworks and industry benchmarks. 
This process was designed to enhance positive externalities, mitigate adverse impacts, and embed resilience 
into our EPC operations.
KPIL will initiate its first -ev er Double Materiality Assessment, integrating both impact materiality (inside-out) and 
financial materiality (outside-in) perspectives. The outcomes will strengthen our ability to identify critical ESG 
risks and opportunities, align disclosures with evolving global reporting standards, and embed sustainability 
deeper into enterprise -wid e decision -mak ing.

ESG APPROACH AND STRATEGY
OUR STRATEGY
IN ACTION
At KPIL, we believe that robust governance is the bedrock of credible and lasting 
sustainability progress. Our ESG governance framework establishes clear 
accountability, structured oversight, and systematic integration of environmental, 
social, and governance considerations into the way we run our business across 
both our Real Estate and EPC verticals.
Effective ESG governance at KPIL is not a parallel or advisory function; it is 
embedded within our enterprise wide risk and strategy processes, ensuring that 
sustainability commitments are owned, monitored, and acted upon at every level 
of the organisation.
Please refer to the sections in our Annual Report titled 'Governance and Risk Oversight' and 'Report on  
Corporate Governance' (on page no. 114  and page no. 179  respectively). These sections collectively provide 
a comprehensive overview of the Company’s governance philosophy, structure, practices, and control 
framework, and reflect the robustness of KPIL’s commitment to transparency, accountability, ethical conduct, 
and regulatory compliance across all levels of the organisation.
OUR ESG GOVERNANCE PHILOSOPHY
KPIL's Approach to ESG Governance Rests on Three Core Principles:
Accountability
Every material ESG topic has a defined owner, ensuring that commitments translate into measurable action.
Transparency
We report our ESG performance with the robust rigour, enabling stakeholders to make informed assessments 
of our progress.
Continuous Improvement
Our ESG governance structures are designed not merely for compliance, but to drive ongoing advancement 
in our sustainability performance, policies, and disclosures.Sustainability Strategy
KPIL’s sustainability strategy is designed to integrate 
environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and 
governance excellence into every aspect of our operations. 
It reflects both continuity and evolution: while we remain 
committed to the core focus areas established in prior 
years, we have incrementally expanded our scope to 
address emerging priorities and stakeholder expectations.
The strategy is structured around three guiding pillars 
that provide clarity of purpose and direction. These pillars 
ensure that our actions are not only aligned with global 
sustainability goals but also tailored to the specific needs of 
our business, communities, and stakeholders. Together, they 
form the foundation of our journey towards long-term value 
creation, resilience and future readiness.

ESG Policies and Commitments
Please refer to the sections in our Annual Reportitled 
'Governance and Risk Oversight' and 'Report on Corporate 
Governance' (on page no. 114  and page no. 179  respectively). 
The aforesaid reports also provide meaningful insights 
into the working and implementation of the Company’s 
governance policies in practice, demonstrating how these 
frameworks are embedded into day to day decision making 
and operational processes across the organisation.
Policy Commitments
Our ESG policies form the cornerstone of our organisational 
framework, reflecting our commitment to ethical business 
practices, respect for human rights, environmental 
stewardship, and strict regulatory compliance. These 
policies guide our strategic decisions and operational 
practices, ensuring that sustainability principles are 
embedded across all aspects of our business.
ESG Risk
KPIL's ESG risk is integrated with our Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework. Any ESG risks that are 
identified and assessed are managed using the same systematic methodology applied to financial and 
operational risks, ensuring parity of rigour and consistent accountability across all risk categories.Embedding Policy Commitments
To ensure effective implementation, we integrate ESG 
commitments through structured induction programmes, 
operational controls, and continuous audit monitoring 
across all functions. Training and awareness initiatives 
reinforce employee accountability, while monitoring 
mechanisms safeguard compliance and performance.

• Phased Work Orders: Redesigned foundation beams and adopted steel composite columns, enabling

seamlessly with Phase -1, a voiding costly modifications to existing shear walls and saving significant 
construction time.

• Steel Composite Column Construction:  Reduced

Driving Efficiency through Lean Construction
At KPIL, timely project delivery has always been a strategic 
priority. To strengthen execution and optimise slab cycle 
times in Building & Factories (B&F) projects, KPIL has 
embraced Lean Construction principles. By deploying 
methodologies such as the Last Planner System (LPS) and 
Pull Planning, we have fostered collaborative planning that 
involves stakeholders at every level, resulting in improved 
coordination, realistic schedules and enhanced ownership 
of outcomes.
On site, lean practices have been embedded through 
daily huddle meetings to remove constraints, backward 
planning from key milestones, visual management boards 
for workfront visibility, and continuous look ahead planning 
with subcontractors. Performance is tracked through 
Percentage Plans Completed (PPC), ensuring accountability 
and driving continuous improvement.
The consistent application of these principles has delivered 
measurable benefits:
• Faster execution of projects with reduced slab cycle 
durations.
• Increased accountability and ownership among teams 
and subcontractors.
• Better coordination across planning, execution, and 
workforce deployment.
• Efficient utilisation of resources, leading to customer 
satisfaction and repeat orders.Pioneering Achievement in  
Transmission Infrastructure
In October 2025, KPIL achieved a landmark milestone by 
becoming the first EPC company in India to successfully 
implement the Double Arm Gin Pole (DAGP) Crane 
System at a transmission line worksite outside China. This 
pioneering achievement marks a significant advancement 
for the Indian power transmission industry.
KPIL successfully erected a 765 kV double circuit 
transmission tower using the DAGP crane, underscoring our 
commitment to engineering excellence and innovation in 
power transmission infrastructure. The introduction of this 
system in India for the first time is poised to transform tower 
erection methodologies, enabling faster, safer, and more 
efficient construction of transmission lines.
During its second deployment, the DAGP system achieved 
a productivity rate of 10.85 MT per day, with the potential to 
scale up to 15 MT per day. This benchmark demonstrates 
KPIL’s forward-looking capabilities and sets new standards 
for efficiency, safety and precision in the industry.
This breakthrough represents a major advancement for 
India’s transmission sector, reaffirming KPIL’s role as a leader 
in innovation and operational excellence. By integrating 
pioneering technologies into our projects, we continue to 
set benchmarks in construction efficiency and contribute to 
building sustainable, future-ready infrastructure.Engineering Excellence in Extreme Conditions
KPIL successfully commissioned one of India’s most 
challenging transmission line projects - the Lakadia–
Ahmedabad TL -01 ( 92.357 km). Execution excellence was 
tested against formidable obstacles including low -ly ing, 
waterlogged terrain, saline creek crossings, severe 
right -of-way constraints, pile foundations, and restricted 
working windows in theft prone areas. Despite these 
complexities, the project was completed within the limited 
workable period while maintaining uncompromising 
standards of safety, quality and execution discipline. 
A standout achievement was the completion of all 20 
pile foundation locations within just 100 days, reflecting 
strong site monitoring and seamless multi agency 
coordination. This milestone reinforces KPIL’s capability to 
deliver complex projects in high risk environments through 
meticulous planning, innovative methodologies and robust 
interfunctional collaboration, thereby strengthening its 
manufactured capital base.

Challenge
The Ground Support System (GSS) originally designed for 
13m piers had to be adapted for 16m piers. The increased 
height created higher loads and stability concerns, 
making direct reuse unsafe.
Solution
KPIL’s design team carried out advanced Finite Element 
Method (FEM) analysis to test the system under new 
conditions. Targeted strengthening and connection 
modifications were introduced, allowing safe reuse of 
the existing GSS without full replacement.NAGPUR METRO – GROUND SUPPORT SYSTEM (GSS)
Impact
• Resource Optimisation:  Reused existing system 
instead of fabricating new. 
• Material Savings:  ~21 MT of structural steel saved.
• Cost Savings:  ~INR 55.92 Lakh avoided.
• Time Efficiency:  Reduced fabrication time and 
ensured timely erection.
• Sustainability:  Minimised waste and promoted 
reuse of resources.

sustainable infrastructure for the future.WATER CONSERV ATION AND TECHNOLOGY UPGRADE  
THROUGH CURING COMPOUNDS
Traditional concrete curing methods rely on continuous 
water application for 14-21 days, consuming large 
volumes of water per slab. In large scale projects, 
this practice places immense pressure on municipal 
water supplies. KPIL identified curing compounds as 
a sustainable alternative, reducing water use while 
maintaining concrete strength and durability.
Implementation
• Deployed curing compounds across multiple 
construction parcels, replacing traditional water 
curing methods.
• Materials included acrylic-based, water-based, and 
advanced formulations such as Fosroc ConCure 
RB90, Fairmate Faircure WC and WR series.• Technology upgrades included drone mapping and 
digital monitoring to track application efficiency 
and ensure uniform curing.
• Total curing compounds used: 3,01,485 litres.
Quantified Outcomes
• Efficiency Gains:  Reduced manual labour and 
dependency on continuous water supply, improving 
operational timelines.
• Community Impact:  Significant reduction in strain 
on local water resources, supporting sustainable 
infrastructure development.
• Quantified Outcomes:  ~3,769,000 litres of water 
conserved across sites.

KalpaGyaan: Knowledge  
Management Platform
KalpaGyaan is KPIL’s in-house Knowledge Management 
platform, developed to capture, store, and share knowledge 
across the organisation. It serves as a central digital library 
where employees can easily access important project 
learnings and technical information.
The platform brings together a wide range of knowledge 
resources such as project learnings, best practices, 
drone videos, standard operating procedures (SOPs), 
work methods, testing standards, training materials, and 
execution processes. It also captures case studies, lessons 
learned, leadership insights, and industry trends, helping 
teams learn from past experiences and improve future 
project execution.
KalpaGyaan also uses Generative AI features to make 
knowledge easier to find and use. These features provide 
better search results, curated insights and multilingual 
support.PORTABLE ACCESS LADDER – IN HOUSE INNOV ATION
Challenge:  Conventional cuplock pipe access systems, 
though widely used, required time consuming erection 
and dismantling, multiple components, and skilled 
labour. This led to higher workman hours and reduced 
efficiency, especially for repetitive access needs 
across  s ites.
Solution:  KPIL’s DCOE EW Heavy Civil Team designed and 
developed a portable ladder system in-house using 
structural steel. The ladder was engineered for:
• Quick assembly and dismantling  with simple bolted 
connections (no welding or special tools).
• Lightweight yet durable construction  for easy 
handling and safe use.
• Reusability and flexibility  across multiple site 
conditions, including direct ground level access.
Impact
• Productivity Gains:  Faster turnaround and reduced 
dependency on skilled labour.
• Efficiency:  Significant savings in workman hours 
and improved coordination at sites.• Cost Savings:  ~INR 20 Lakh saved compared to 
conventional systems.
• Sustainability:  Modular, reusable design 
reduced material usage and promoted resource 
optimisation.
Highlight
By replacing conventional scaffolding with a modular, 
portable ladder system, KPIL demonstrated how 
in-house innovation can deliver safer, faster, and 
more cost-effective solutions while enhancing site 
productivity.

West BengalKalpataru Skill Development Academy 
Kalpataru Skill Development Academy (KSDA) was 
launched by Kalpataru Projects International Limited during 
FY 2023-24 with the aim of addressing the skill shortage in 
the EPC sector. The academy focuses on nurturing young 
talent by providing essential technical competencies that 
improve employability and support the development of a 
skilled workforce.
To ensure high-quality and industry relevant training, KSDA 
works closely with a wide range of partners, including 
Government ITIs, PARFI, CIDC, NGOs, and local institutions. 
By utilising existing infrastructure and aligning programmes 
with industry requirements, KSDA delivers effective and 
standardised training opportunities. 
Human Capital Strategy
KPIL’s approach to human capital development is 
designed to take shape well before employees transition 
into managerial positions. The Company sources early 
career talent from a broad and diverse institutional 
ecosystem spanning National Institutes of Technology 
(NITs), specialised construction and infrastructure institutes 
such as NICMAR, state engineering colleges, Chartered 
Accountancy and Cost & Management Accountancy 
streams, and government polytechnics across India. 
The Company focuses on building a strong internal pipeline 
enabling progress alongside a deep understanding of 
organisational values, business context, and institutional 
knowledge. This philosophy is embedded across 
four structured transition milestones that guide the 
employee  l ifecycle:Training Framework and Programme Offerings
KSDA operates through two core training streams, namely, 
Fresh Skilling and Upskilling (On-the-Job Training – OJT). 
Fresh Skilling blends centre-based theoretical learning with 
structured on-site exposure for unemployed youth, while 
Upskilling focuses on enhancing competencies of existing 
workmen through practical, site-based training.
In FY 2025-26, KSDA further strengthened its training 
framework by standardising On-the-Job Training 
(OJT) modules across projects. Trade specific curricula 
and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) were 
developed and implemented across Water, Buildings 
& Factories (B&F), and Urban Infrastructure divisions, 
ensuring a consistent, site-ready workforce aligned with 
operational  r equirements.

have been trained under Fresh Skilling programmes 
while over 8,000 workers have benefitted from Upskilling 
initiatives. These programmes have directly contributed to 
improved employability, higher productivity, enhanced site 
performance, and increased income levels for participants.
During FY 2025-26, KSDA successfully trained over 
400+ unemployed youth in industry critical trades and 
facilitated their deployment across KPIL project sites. 
Additionally, more than 5,000 existing workers received 
structured OJT to bridge key skill gaps. Individual 
success stories further underscore programme 
effectiveness. Four KSDA trained candidates were 
elevated to Quality Supervisor roles in the T&D Nagpur 
Project, while two candidates progressed from workmen 
to Supervisor positions in the West India Operations 
(WIO) and North India Operations (NIO) divisions.
Geographic Expansion and Partnerships
KSDA has expanded its footprint across Bihar and West 
Bengal, creating meaningful socioeconomic impact 
by empowering local communities. KSDA significantly 
expanded its institutional partnerships by signing an MoU 
with the West Bengal Directorate of Industrial Training 
(DIT), enabling access to ITI infrastructure across the state. 
Additionally, KSDA entered MoUs with multiple training 
partners to establish and operate KSDA Training Centres 
across the country, enhancing scalability and cost 
efficiency.
Way forward In West Bengal, KPIL has entered into 
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Sagardighi Government ITI, Murshidabad, Kalyani Government 
ITI, Nadia & Habibpur Government ITI, Malda. These 
collaborations focus on skilling youth in key construction 
trades and strengthening regional employability.
New training centers were operationalised during the year 
in Assam (Kokrajhar and Tinsukia), Jharkhand (Hazaribagh), 
and Bihar (Darbhanga and Gaya). These centres, fully 
managed by training partners, are actively delivering skill 
training aligned with KPIL project requirements.
Technology and Innovation
KSDA continued its journey of digital transformation in 
FY 2025-26 through the integration of technology driven 
training management systems. Digital data capture for 
OJT was initiated using a WhatsApp chatbot to improve 
real-time reporting and tracking. The Kalp Kushal Portal was 
established to capture detailed workmen profiles, including 
trade competencies and skill levels, while the Learning 
Management System (LMS) now hosts standardised 
training modules accessible across locations. 
Monitoring
KSDA employs a robust performance measurement 
framework and mechanism to assess programme 
effectiveness. In FY 2025-26, Fresh Skilling programmes were 
evaluated based on average cost per trainee, post-training 
deployment retention, and performance assessments 
from site teams. OJT programmes were assessed through 
structured trainee and trainer feedback in addition to 
'Value Addition Reports' submitted by site leadership to 
measure operational and commercial impact. Operational 
challenges were addressed under programmes to ensure 
transparency and stakeholder alignment. OUTLOOK
This year marked strong operational and scale 
efficiencies for KSDA. The Academy achieved a 40% 
reduction in Fresh Skilling costs compared to the 
previous year while successfully deploying over 400 
fresh candidates. More than 5,000 workmen were 
trained through OJT, and an internal certification 
programme was introduced to standardise skill 
validation across projects.
Upskilling initiatives continued to scale across 48 
project sites covering East India Operations (EIO), 
WIO, South India Operations (SIO), Water, and Urban 
Infrastructure divisions under the programme KSDA 
also enabled international workforce mobility by 
sponsoring 250 diploma students for Oil & Gas 
projects in Saudi Arabia and deploying trained 
technicians to projects in Chile, underscoring KSDA’s 
alignment with global project requirements and 
quality benchmarks. 
Looking ahead, KSDA plans to focus strongly 
on expanding OJT and strengthening digital 
monitoring. The Academy aims to achieve the 
following in the upcoming financial year:

across the Buildings & Factories, Water, and 
Transmission & Distribution (T&D) divisions in 
India. 
• Digitalisation: OJT framework will be digitalised

performance tracking and adherence to First 
Time Right (FTR) standards. 
• Candidate Deployment:  KSDA targets the

strengthening the pipeline of site-ready talent. 
Together, these initiatives position KSDA to deepen 
its operational impact, enhance transparency 
and efficiency, and support KPIL’s growth through

improvement in EHS performance.

Environment, Health, and Safety (EHS) 
Practices and Initiatives 
At KPIL, EHS is embedded into everyday operations through 
well-defined policies and procedures, reinforced by 
structured risk assessments to systematically identify 
and control potential hazards. Our workforce is supported 
through comprehensive EHS training programmes 
that build safety awareness and capability, along with 
occupational health services such as on-site medical 
facilities, routine health screenings, and employee 
wellness  in itiatives.Occupational health and safety are managed through 
established practices including Hazard Identification 
and Risk Assessment (HIRA) and detailed Root Cause 
Analysis. Our ISO 45001:2018 certification and EHSS Policy 
underline a strong focus on process efficiency, technology 
adoption, and behavioural transformation. These efforts 
are structured around nine strategic pillars that collectively 
promote a strong and sustainable safety culture across 
all o perations.
Monitoring for EHS Excellence
We leverage real-time monitoring to track EHS performance 
across project sites, supported by daily data collection and 
monthly Rapid Quantitative EHS Assessments to identify 
trends and initiate timely corrective actions. Quarterly 
performance reviews are shared with senior leadership.
Building a Culture of Safety
KPIL delivers comprehensive EHS training to all employees 
and contractors through regular workshops, toolbox talks, 
and behaviour-based safety sessions. The Behaviour Based 
Safety (BBS) programme strengthens a shared safety 
culture, supported by emergency preparedness drills and 
the Safety Passport Programme to ensure competency in 
operational areas.
Incident Management
Root cause investigations are conducted using the ‘5 Why’ 
methodology, and key learnings are disseminated through 
the Knowledge Management System to prevent recurrence 
and maintain consistent safety performance.
Technology and Innovation in EHS
Digital tools further enhance safety visibility and 
responsiveness. The EHS app enables real -tim e incident 
reporting, while AI -ena bled analytics identify PPE 
non-compliance to support immediate corrective action 
and reinforce KPIL’s commitment to achieving Zero Harm.
EHS Monitoring 
We promote accountability and continuous improvement 
in EHS performance through a structured, multi-level 
review and framework. A robust three-tier audit system is 
carried out by site-level EHS teams, business unit teams, 
and the corporate EHS function ensures comprehensive 
evaluation and effective cross-verification of safety 
practices. EHS Steering Committees function across 
different organisational levels to provide consistent 
oversight, while monthly EHS Snapshots help keep 
leadership informed and aligned.
Senior management regularly conducts site 
walk -arounds to engage with project teams and identify opportunities for improvement. Fortnightly 
review calls with EHS leaders are held to assess key 
performance indicators and track progress on safety 
initiatives, supported by periodic fire safety audits to 
proactively address risks. Quarterly EHS Council Meetings 
enable in-depth performance reviews and strategic 
planning. Strengthening this monitoring structure, 
competency mapping and external skill assessments 
ensure that EHS personnel remain well-equipped and 
capable of meeting evolving safety requirements.

Education
KPIL views education as a key driver of long term social 
and economic development and focuses its CSR efforts 
on reducing the digital divide, improving STEM learning, 
and strengthening teaching quality. The Company 
upgraded educational infrastructure by introducing 
Digital Smart Classrooms in 15 schools, benefiting 
more than 4,500 students and training 196 teachers 
in technology enabled pedagogy. KPIL also upgraded 
Typing Labs into Advanced Computer Labs at IERT, 
Prayagraj to enhance digital proficiency and support 
technical education.
To promote experiential learning, a hub and spoke STEM 
intervention was launched across six rural schools 
in Raipur District, with a state-of-the-art STEM Lab 
established at the hub school in Khorpa village and 
extended to five spoke schools. This initiative engaged 
2,001 students through 869 hands-on sessions, 
strengthening foundational skills in science and 
mathematics.
Restoring Mobility, Renewing Dignity
Yug Mangal*, a 76-year-old resident of Antichak village, 
Bhagalpur District, Bihar, approached the Mobile 
Medical Unit (MMU) suffering from intense lower back 
pain that was limiting his ability to carry out daily 
activities. After a thorough clinical evaluation, he was 
diagnosed with arthritis. The medical team prescribed 
suitable medication and advised him on gentle 
physical exercises and proper dietary practices.
Through consistent follow-ups and strict adherence to 
the treatment regimen, his pain steadily diminished and 
his mobility improved markedly. This support helped 
him regain ease in his everyday life, underscoring the 
vital role of accessible healthcare services for elderly 
individuals in rural communities.From Problem to Prototype
Master Maurya Sahu*, a Class 6 student from Chandi 
village in Raipur district, Chhattisgarh turned a personal 
challenge related to water shortage into a thoughtful 
innovation. Observing his mother’s daily hardship 
in collecting water motivated him to seek solutions 
during his STEM classes. Applying his understanding of 
renewable energy and conservation, Maurya developed 
a functional rainwater harvesting model that illustrated 
how rainwater can be efficiently collected, stored, 
and reused. With support from his STEM mentor, he 
successfully constructed and presented the model, 
effectively connecting classroom concepts to a 
real-life problem. His effort earned him the chance 
to showcase the project at a State-level Science 
Exhibition, highlighting the powerful impact of hands-on 
STEM  l earning.

KPIL highly prioritises sustainable sourcing to ensure our 
supply chain is adaptable and socially responsible. With 
customers increasingly valuing sustainability, we strive 
to deliver quality beyond the compliance standards. 
Therefore, we integrate sustainability into our procurement 
processes to meet stakeholder expectations and positively 
impact society and the environment.
Our sustainable procurement process is structured around 
three core stages:
• RFQ Management: Ensuring fair, transparent, and 
sustainability informed sourcing through structured 
evaluation and selection of vendors.
• Value Engineering: Applying value engineering 
principles to optimise costs and enhance product 
functionality while maintaining quality and reducing 
environmental impact.
• Order Execution:  Ensuring efficient and timely 
execution of orders in a manner consistent with KPIL's 
sustainability standards and client expectations.

approach reinforces our commitment to reducing our

Every year we undertake a GHG Inventorisation study to 
understand and map the sources of our Scope 1, 2 and 3 
emissions. Our Scope 1 emissions include emissions from 
diesel, LPG, propane, petrol and PNG consumption, while our 
Scope 2 include purchased electricity. Scope 3 Emissions 
arise from:Emission Reduction and  
Decarbonisation Strategies
KPIL has adopted a structured and forward -lo oking 
approach to emission reduction and decarbonisation, 
ensuring that our business operations align with global 
climate goals and stakeholder expectations. Our strategy 
is built on the principle of the mitigation hierarchy to avoid, 
reduce, replace, neutralise with a clear focus on absolute 
reductions in Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions before 
offsetting residuals.
Basis of GHG Reporting
Our Greenhouse Gas (GHG) inventory for FY 2025-26 has 
been prepared in accordance with the GHG Protocol 
Corporate Standard, covering all material Scope 1, 2, and 3 
emissions since we began this process in FY 2023-24.
Consolidation Approach:  We account for emissions 
based on the operational control approach. To prevent 
double counting, emissions from internal transactions and 
activities already accounted for in Scope 1 and 2 have been 
excluded from our Scope 3 calculations.
Methodologies & Emission Factors:  Our inventory is 
based on activity data from our operations and a hybrid 
methodology for our supply chain. Emission factors and 
Global Warming Potential (GWP) values are sourced from 
the latest available, internationally recognised databases: 
Scope 1:  Factors for fossil fuel combustion are from the GHG 
Protocol's 'Emission Factors for Cross-Sector Tools (v2.0),  
with GWP values for converting CH4 and N2O to CO2e taken 
from the GHG Protocol's August 2024 guidance .
Scope 2:  India's Central Electricity Authority (CEA) database 
(v21.0)  provides the grid electricity emission factor.
Scope 3:  For Scope 3, we utilised a hybrid methodology 
combining spend-based and weight-based calculations 
for our largest emissions category, Purchased Goods and 
Services. Emission factors were sourced from a range of 
credible, publicly available databases, including: the UK 
DEFRA 2025 Greenhouse Gas Reporting: Conversion Fators 
(for fuel, transport, and waste).
MoEFCC CCTS notifications and World Steel Association 
data for vendor-specific emissions from the Ion & Steel 
sector.
US EPA's EEIO  database for spend-based calculations, 
normalised for India using the World Bank's Purchasing 
Power Parity (PPP) conversion factor.Global Cement and Concrete Association (GCCA) data for 
the cement sector.  Blended Cement - Green, Durable & 
Sustainable
This structured approach ensures that our emissions 
inventory is transparent, consistent, and aligned with global 
best practices.
Note: In line with GHG Protocol standards, CO2 emissions from the 
combustion of biomass are calculated and reported separately from 
our Scope 1, 2 and 3. The associated non-CO2 emissions (CH4 and N2O) 
from biomass combustion are included within our Scope 1 inventory, 
using emission factors UK DEFRA 2025 Greenhouse Gas Reporting .  
Note: The consumption of Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS) is not 
considered material to our operations as an EPC business.

Verified Emissions (Scope 1 & 2):  10,971.09  t CO2e
Carbon Credits Retired:  11,600  t CO2e (high quality, 
independently-verified)
Neutrality Achieved:  100% carbon neutrality for TLI 
operations
Our carbon neutrality approach is aligned with 
global frameworks such as the Science Based 
Targets initiative (SBTi) and the Task Force on 
Climate Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). We 
follow the recognised mitigation hierarchy of 'avoid-
reduce-replace-neutralise', applying carbon credits 
only after implementing practicable emission 
reduction measures. This disciplined approach 
ensures that offsets are used solely for residual 
Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.
Carbon credits were procured under internationally 
recognised standards such as Verified Carbon 
Standard (VCS), Gold Standard (GS), and 
Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), with 
a strong preference for projects located in 
India to strengthen local climate action and 
deliver co -be nefits. KPIL prioritised renewable 
energy and energy efficiency projects with 
proven additionality, credible baselines, and 
independent verification, ensuring environmental 
integrity and stakeholder confidence.
Through this structured and transparent 
methodology, KPIL demonstrates that carbon 
credits are not substitutes for emission reduction 
but a strategic interim mechanism to address 
residual emissions. This achievement underscores 
our leadership in responsible climate action 
and strengthens our competitiveness in global 
EPC ma rkets.NATURAL CAPITAL

Water Risk Assessment
As one of India’s largest engineering and construction 
companies, we recognise that managing water risks 
is critical to ensuring sustainable business practices 
and safeguarding stakeholder interests. We continue to 
strengthen our resilience against water -re lated challenges 
through a comprehensive risk assessment framework. 
Our assessment focused on identifying potential impacts 
of water scarcity, flooding, and water quality issues across 
global operations. Using advanced tools such as the 
WWF Water Risk Filter, we categorised risks into physical, 
regulatory, and reputational dimensions, enabling us to 
prioritise high-risk sites and implement targeted mitigation 
measures. This process also included measuring our water 
footprint by tracking consumption, wastewater generation, 
and recycling practices, aligning with our long -te rm goal of 
becoming water-positive by 2032.
To achieve this ambition, we are expanding initiatives 
such as rainwater harvesting, wastewater reuse, and 
deployment of water -ef ficient technologies across facilities 
and project sites. We continue to adopt international 
standards like ISO 46001 for water -ef ficient management 
systems and actively participate in CDP Water Security 
Ratings, reinforcing transparency and accountability in 
our d isclosures.
Our approach integrates boundary setting for risk 
assessments, regular reviews of existing practices, and 
proactive mitigation strategies. By reducing dependency on 
freshwater resources and strengthening compliance with 
local regulations, KPIL is not only safeguarding operations 
but also contributing positively to the communities and 
ecosystems in which we operate.
Water Stewardship and Reuse
In FY 2025–26, we continued to sustain the initiatives 
implemented at our Gandhinagar Plant to achieve Zero 
Liquid Discharge. Through measures such as area -wis e 
water consumption monitoring, automated tank level 
controllers, leakage prevention, and the operation of a 50 
KLD Sewage Treatment Plant, we ensured that treated water 
was consistently reused for toilet flushing and gardening.
While no new projects were added during the year, our 
focus remained on maintaining operational efficiency and 
reinforcing water circularity. These efforts helped us sustain 
high levels of process water reuse and domestic water 
reuse, thereby minimising wastage and strengthening our 
commitment to environmental stewardship.NATURAL CAPITAL
Waste Management and  
Circular Economy
We place waste management at the heart of our project 
design, ensuring reduction, recycling, and reuse are 
embedded from the very beginning. Our biomass plants 
continue to support thousands of farmer families by 
sustainably managing agricultural residue, transforming 
what was once a disposal challenge into a valuable input 
that prevents stubble burning and reduces air pollution. 
Across construction sites, we have advanced circular 
practices by repurposing slump tested concrete into cover 
blocks, reusing discarded cubes for walls and boundary 
structures, and converting waste concrete into functional 
applications such as drain covers, sleepers, crash barriers, 
and even landscaping elements. Steel scrap is recovered 
through bar straightening machines, extending the lifecycle 
of materials and reducing demand for fresh inputs. Fly ash 
and other recycled materials are deployed in civil works, 
further minimising environmental impact.
At every site, waste segregation is a standard practice, 
enabling proper sorting for recycling and safe disposal. 
Hazardous waste is managed responsibly through 
authorised vendors in line with regulatory requirements, 
while non -ha zardous waste is recycled wherever feasible. 
Contractors are incentivised to recover and recycle building 
materials, creating both environmental and financial value. 
By following the 3R hierarchy — Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. KPIL 
is not only minimising landfill dependency but also creating 
value -added products, recovering energy from waste, and 
embedding circular economy principles into infrastructure 
development. This integrated approach reflects our 
commitment to innovation, compliance, and sustainability, 
ensuring that waste is transformed into opportunity and 
long -term value.TURNING WASTE INTO

Waste Footprint Assessment
KPIL continues to advance its commitment to sustainability 
and the principles of a circular economy through a 
comprehensive Waste Footprint Assessment (WFA). This 
initiative enables us to quantify and characterise waste 
generated across operations, identify gaps, and strengthen 
our waste management practices.
Recognising the environmental impact of resource 
extraction and processing, KPIL applies a waste 
management hierarchy that prioritises minimisation, reuse, 
recycling, and energy recovery. The current WFA covers nine 
divisions of our direct operations, with clear boundaries set 
to estimate waste generation and assess the proportion 
reused, recycled, and safely disposed of.
The assessment revealed opportunities for improvement, 
including the need for a formal waste management policy 
and enhanced tracking mechanisms. In response, KPIL is 
developing a robust waste management policy, adopting 
standardised templates for waste inventories, and setting 
ambitious recycling and reuse targets. Our long term goal 
is to achieve 100% circularity in construction and demolition 
waste by 2035, supported by certifications such as Zero 
Waste to Landfill. A mechanism is being introduced to 
monitor progress and allocate budgets for recycling 
projects.
We are actively pursuing sustainable waste management 
by designing out waste and optimising material use. Key 
actions include designing for reuse and recovery, offsite 
construction, material optimisation, and waste efficient 
procurement. Advanced technologies such as wet and dry 
processing of construction and demolition waste are being 
explored to produce aggregates and sand for construction 
activities. In addition, KPIL is committed to sustainable 
practices for managing food waste, plastic waste, e waste, 
and metal waste, through composting, plastic granulation, 
and modular design for electronic products.

BIOMASS DIVISION INITIATIVES
Electricity ProductionEnergy Efficiency & Renewable Initiatives 
Padampur Power Plant (PPP)
Installation of Motorised Rotary  
Soot Blower (RSB) 
The manual and mechanically operated soot blower for 
super heater tubes has been replaced with a motorised 
system. This upgrade enables easier, more precise 
operation and effective ash deposit removal from boiler 
tubes. It delivers qualitative improvements through its 
automatic activation during set durations under routine 
operations.Uniara Power Plant (UPP)
Installation of 15 TPH Capacity Soil  
Separator (Trommel) System 
Agricultural fuel contains high dust levels, exacerbated 
by adulteration, which increases boiler maintenance 
frequency and decreases boiler efficiency. To mitigate 
this, we have enhanced our soil separation capacity 
by adding a parallel 15 TPH Trommel unit to the existing 
6 TPH asset. This upgrade fully meets the boiler's daily 
processed fuel requirements.Padampur Power Plant (PPP)
Modification in Central Cooling  
AC Water Supply 
The Variable Refrigerant Volume (VRV) unit is installed 
for maintaining the air conditioning in the Control Room. 
Its water-cooled condenser unit discharge line has a 
separate pump for circulating water in the loop. Now, this 
unit has been connected to the existing Auxiliary Cooling 
Water Pump’s discharge line. This modification eliminates 
the need for the 3.7 kW AC water pump, especially during 
winter season, resulting in energy savings.  This initiative reflects the principle of process 
optimisation, where energy demand is reduced by 
aligning operations with seasonal requirements.
Impacts
• Energy Savings:  15,120 kWh annually
• Operational Benefit : Simplified cooling operations, 
reduced wear and tear, and improved system 
reliability.
Uniara Power Plant (UPP)
Installation of Air Compressor Units with VSD  
Two old, inefficient air compressors with new units 
having a volumetric flow rate of 125 CFM. Both 
compressors are equipped with in built Variable 
Speed Drives (VSD), enabling optimisation of power 
consumption according to demand. Each unit delivers 
a saving of 9 kW, reflecting the principle of variable load 
management, where equipment adjusts energy use 
based on operational requirements.
• Energy Savings:  75,600 kWh annually
• Impact:  Improved compressor efficiency, reduced 
operational costs, and stabilised air supply.
Energy Efficient Main Cooling Water Pump  
A 90 kW pump was replaced with a 75 kW energy 
efficient pump, delivering the same flow rate. This 
demonstrates technology substitution, where modern, 
efficient equipment replaces legacy systems to reduce 
energy intensity.
• Energy Savings:  76,800 kWh annually
• Impact:  Lowered pump energy intensity, reduced 
maintenance, and enhanced cooling reliability.Replacement of Cooling Tower Fan Blades  
Lightweight E glass epoxy blades replaced conventional 
FRP blades, reducing fan load by 7 kW. This initiative 
is an example of material innovation, where 
advanced materials improve efficiency and durability 
simultaneously.
• Energy Savings:  53,760 kWh annually
• Impact:  Reduced fan load, improved cooling 
efficiency, and extended equipment life.
Both PPP and UPP plants have implemented energy 
efficiency initiatives to reduce auxiliary consumption. 
These include installing LED street lights, replacing 
conventional motors with energy -ef ficient IE3/IE4 motors, 
and deploying BLDC fans. Collectively, these measures 
enhance operational efficiency and contribute to 
long -term carbon emission reduction.0102

Power Plant
  3 MWp (AC) Solar PV Power Plant has been installed 
to supplement the existing 8 MW biomass-based 
power plant at UPP. This has reduced the net carbon 
emission from the plant’s overall electricity export 
to the grid, as a portion of the biomass generation 
load is shifted to Solar PV plant during daytime.
  Impacts:  The solar plant generated 5,125 MWh 
annually, exporting 5,050 MWh to the grid. This 
aligns with the theory of renewable substitution, 
where clean energy displaces fossil fuel based 
electricity, reducing overall carbon footprint and 
strengthening renewable portfolio, supporting long 
term climate goals and stakeholder value creation.
ii  Purchased two Electric Vehicle cars to 
reduce carbon emissions and promote 
sustainable transport.
iii  Reduction of SPM levels and Carbon 
Capture from flue gases 
   M/s E-Neuf Green Solutions Private Limited, Jaipur 
has been appointed to carry out the R&D for this 
initiative. For this, a stream (through the tapping 
taken from the main flue gas duct) has been made 
to pass through two tanks containing chemical 
solvent (for SPM reduction) and algae (for Carbon 
Capture). Trials are currently underway, with the 
potential to significantly mitigate emissions from 
biomass operations.

06UPP
Procurement of Flash Air Dryer
Biomass is procured mostly during the Rabi Season 
(Springs) and stored into the land facility. Despite being 
covered, it remains exposed to weather conditions all 
year round; it undergoes cyclical changes especially with 
respect to its moisture content. 
To control moisture before feeding biomass into the 
Boiler System, we are installing a Flash Air Dryer with 
a throughput capacity of 3 MT per hour. This system is 
expected to reduce the moisture content in the output 
by 10–12%, thereby lowering the overall moisture in the 
fuel supplied to the Boiler. As a result, we anticipate 
achieving more stable combustion in the Boiler 
Furnace and a reduced frequency of load reductions.

Rajasthan. Under the Rajasthan Factory Safety Awards 
Scheme 2026, the plant secured award under category 
of 'medium' scale factory on occasion of 55th National 
Safety Day Celebration, showcasing our ongoing 
commitment to maintaining the safety standards 
within the plant.Biodiversity Conservation and Restoration

TAT for Shareholder query resolution
The Company is committed to maintaining effective 
investor services and ensuring timely resolution of 
shareholders’ queries, grievances, and requests. The 
Shareholder-related communications received directly or 
through various channels including Registrar and Share 
Transfer Agent (RTA), e-mails, SEBI SCORES, Smart ODR 
platform and stock exchanges are regularly monitored and 
addressed in a prompt and efficient manner.
During the financial year under review, all shareholder 
queries, requests, and grievances received by the 
Company were resolved within the prescribed statutory 
timelines. The Registrar and Share Transfer Agent (RTA) of 
the Company follows a well-defined internal Turnaround 
Time (TAT) framework, wherein regular shareholder 
correspondences are generally addressed within 10 days, 
while SEBI complaints/Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) 
matters are resolved generally within 3 days from the date 
of receipt, subject to receipt of complete documents/
information. Further, all investor grievances were resolved 
within the maximum prescribed timeline of 21 days, and no 
investor grievance remained pending as on the close of the 
financial  year.General Communications  
with Shareholders
The Company continued to strengthen its engagement 
with shareholders through various investor-centric 
communication initiatives during the year, in addition to 
circulation of the Annual Report. These communications, 
inter-alia , included intimation of special window for re-
lodgement of transfer requests of physical shares, MCA 
initiative under the 100 days Campaign - 'Saksham 
Niveshak', special window for transfer and dematerialisation 
of physical securities, reminder for claiming unclaimed/
unpaid dividend from the Company; claiming shares 
lying in unclaimed suspense account with the Company; 
dematerialisation of shares, updating e-mail address, 
PAN, bank account details and Nomination details. In 
accordance with the SEBI Circulars, the Company has sent 
reminder, to its shareholders intimating them to furnish 
valid PAN, Nomination, Contact details, Mobile Number, 
Specimen Signature, updated Bank Account details for 
receiving dividend electronically.This section describes the systems and processes established to identify, assess, mitigate,

mechanisms implemented to safeguard organisational interests and strengthen

internal control of identified risks were presented to the Committee from time to time.
